Thanks for the ping, Sean. Quick initial security stance and questions below — please note these are gating for legal sign-off: 

1) Definitions: we need "aggregated, non-identifiable analytics" defined explicitly in the DPA. Examples: daily counters, histogram aggregates, cohorted embeddings where no per-user mapping exists.

2) Embeddings: product must confirm whether embeddings are deterministic and whether any salt or transformation is applied. If embeddings are deterministic per input we consider them higher risk. We will require a documented privacy review if embeddings are exported off-platform.

3) Subprocessors: list ALL subprocessors involved in telemetry path (metrics collection, metrics storage, analytics ETL). Acme's redline asks for an allowlist; we prefer to provide a current list and a 30-day notice for additions.

4) Retention & access: any exported data to Snowflake must have a retention cap (we suggest 90 days for raw counters, 365 for aggregated metrics) and RBAC limiting who can access raw exports. We need proof that exported data is encrypted and access is logged.

5) Forbidden items: request-level payloads, raw prompt text, or any PII cannot be exported. If debug logs exist that include user-provided text, those must be redacted.

I attached a short security_evaluation_matrix.xlsx we can fill jointly — Priyom, please populate the product-answers column with the technical details (how embeddings produced, caching behavior, audit log retention, encryption). Once complete, security can convert these into suggested DPA language.

- Olga

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Telemetry & analytics export scoping for DPA — product details and proposed wording

Thanks — wrote up product details below to fill security's matrix: 

- What we emit today: anonymized usage counters (endpoint, model version, token counts), cohorted embedding aggregates (we emit averaged vectors per cohort for internal model evaluation), and latency metrics. We do NOT export raw prompt text or full per-request response bodies to external analytics buckets by default.

- Embeddings characteristics: embeddings are deterministic given identical input and model version. We run an optional salt+noise transform for experimental runs but not for production by default. This means exported embeddings could theoretically be correlated if Acme retains mapping to original inputs. Product recommends the DPA require exported embeddings be aggregated (e.g., averaged by cohort >10 members) and forbids storing per-request embedding vectors tied to identifiers.

- Subprocessor list (current): Google Cloud Storage (metrics export bucket), Segment (metrics routing), Snowflake (customer destination). We can provide a live list and a 30-day notice for additions.

Proposed DPA language (suggested short paragraph for legal to insert): 
"Customer-Allowed Analytics Exports: Redwood may export aggregated, non-identifiable analytics to Customer-controlled analytics destinations (e.g., Snowflake) provided the exported data does NOT contain raw prompt text, per-request response payloads, or identifiers that enable re-identification of individual users. Aggregated embeddings are permitted only when computed over cohorts with a minimum size of 10 and where no mapping to original inputs is retained by the Customer. Redwood will provide a current list of subprocessors and notify Customer 30 days prior to adding new subprocessors that affect telemetry exports."

If security is comfortable with the cohort threshold and retention caps (I suggest product accepts 90 days for raw counters, 365 for aggregated), we can propose this language back to Acme. Olga — can you confirm whether the cohort >=10 rule and the retention windows are acceptable from a security perspective or if you need stronger constraints?

- Priyom
Senior Product Manager, Serving Runtime
